verifications.claim: Jonathan Young is returning for Survivor 50: In the Hands of the Fans.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Jonathan Young... is among the 24 returning castaways competing in Survivor 50: In the Hands of the Fans" (R1/R2); "Jonathan Young is a contestant from Survivor 42 and Survivor 50: In the Hands of the Fans" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm Jonathan Young's return for Survivor 50 with the exact subtitle.

verifications.claim: Survivor 50: In the Hands of the Fans premieres in February 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "premieres Wednesday, Feb. 25, on CBS and Paramount +" (R1/R2)
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify premiere date as Feb. 25, which is in February 2026.

verifications.claim: Jonathan Young finished in 4th place in his first season.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "placed fourth after 25 days" (R1/R2); "finishing in fourth place on Survivor season 42" (R3); "finished in fourth place... Eliminated, Day 25" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources directly state he finished fourth in Survivor 42.

verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "Young, 31," (R3); "Age: 29" (CBS profile for S42, R4); "Age: 32" (EW for S50, R4)
verifications.reasoning: Age 29 was for Survivor 42 (2022); current sources for Survivor 50 (2026) list 31 or 32, contradicting present-tense claim.

verifications.claim: Jonathan Young is an Alabama native.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Alabama's Jonathan Young... hailing from Gulf Shores" (R1/R2); "Hometown: Gadsden, AL... Gulf Shores, AL" (R4); "Jonathan Young of Gulf Shores" (R5/R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently identify him as from Alabama (Gulf Shores/Gadsden).

verifications.claim: Jonathan Young is an NGO worker.

verifications.claim: Jonathan Young trained with Boston Rob for four years to improve his strategic game for this second chance.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "worked with 'Boston Rob' Mariano for years to enhance his strategic gameplay... 'For four years, I went to his house... my strategic game needed some work'" (R3); "Mr. Rob (Boston Rob) is one of my good friends now. He has been such a huge help" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: R3 directly states four years of training with Rob specifically for strategic improvement ahead of S50.

verifications.claim: Jonathan Young trained for four years under Boston Rob Mariano.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "For four years, I went to his house, trained, sat at his feet" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Direct quote confirms four years of training under Boston Rob.

verifications.claim: Jonathan Young aims to balance his known physical threat status with a more improved under-the-radar social strategy.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "physical challenge threat... work on his social and psychological game... play a different game... under-the-radar? 'I want them to think I don't have a strategic bone in my body'" (R3/R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm physical threat reputation and intent to improve social/strategic game to appear less strategic, but not precisely 'under-the-radar social strategy' balancing.

verifications.claim: Jonathan Young expressed a desire to correct mistakes from his previous season.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "I learned a lot from what I did right and wrong in season 42... talking to him about what I could do differently" (R3); "Survivor 42 opened my eyes to different things that helped me grow" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Direct references to learning from mistakes and doing things differently in prior season.

verifications.claim: Jonathan Young expressed a desire to redeem himself after losing in the final four fire-making challenge.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "determined to turn his near-miss into victory... fell short in the fire-making challenge" (R1/R2); "after finishing in fourth place" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources note fire-making loss and determination for victory, implying redemption but not explicitly 'redeem himself'.
